rows.CVE Description:
Summary



CVE-2026-35433 is an Improper Input Validation and Privilege Escalation vulnerability affecting Microsoft .NET when specific settings are enabled. The vulnerability allows an unauthorized adversary to elevate privileges locally on the affected system. Successful exploitation requires the adversary to have local access to the device and user interaction, such as opening a malicious file. The vulnerability impacts systems running vulnerable versions of the .NET framework, primarily affecting workstations and servers where .NET applications are deployed. Upon successful exploitation, an adversary can gain elevated privileges on the local system, potentially achieving higher levels of access than originally granted.



Exploitability




Exploit status: Unproven

Exploit reliability: No public information is available regarding the consistency or reliability of exploitation attempts for this vulnerability



Exploit Requirements





Location: On device. The vulnerability can be exploited with local access to the affected device. The adversary must be able to execute code or interact with the system locally rather than remotely over a network.




Privileges: None. The adversary does not need any authentication or prior access to the system beyond basic local access. The vulnerability can be exploited without any credentials or established sessions, though the adversary must be able to interact with the local system.




User interaction: Required (open file). The vulnerability requires user interaction to be successfully exploited. A user must perform an action such as opening a malicious file or document that triggers the vulnerability, allowing the adversary to elevate privileges on the system.




Conditions: The affected system must have specific non-default settings enabled for the vulnerability to be exploitable. The exact configuration requirements are not publicly detailed, but the vulnerability does not affect default installations of .NET.




Affected Products




Microsoft .NET



Mitigations




Review any recommended remediations

rows.CVE Description:
Summary



CVE-2026-32175 is a Tampering vulnerability affecting Microsoft .NET Core. An adversary who successfully exploits this vulnerability could write arbitrary files and directories to certain locations on a vulnerable system, though with limited control over the destination. The vulnerability requires the adversary to send a specially crafted file to the target system. Successful exploitation results in the ability to tamper with files on the affected system, potentially compromising system integrity. This vulnerability affects servers and workstations running .NET Core applications.



Exploitability




Exploit status: Unproven

Exploit details: The vulnerability is exploited by sending a specially crafted file to a .NET Core application. When the application improperly handles this file, the adversary can write arbitrary files and directories to certain locations on the system. The adversaryâ€™s control over the destination of these files and directories is limited, restricting the scope of potential tampering operations.



Exploit Requirements




Location: Remote. The vulnerability can be exploited remotely by an adversary who can send specially crafted files to the target system over the network, without requiring local access to the affected device.

Privileges: Low. The adversary requires low-level authentication or prior access to the system to send the specially crafted file to the vulnerable .NET Core application.

User interaction: None. The vulnerability does not require any action from users of the affected system. The adversary can trigger the vulnerability directly by sending a specially crafted file to the application without requiring users to click links, open files, or perform any other actions that would facilitate the attack.

Conditions: The affected system must be running a .NET Core application that processes files in a manner that triggers the improper file handling behavior.



Affected Products




Microsoft .NET Core



Mitigations




Review any recommended remediations

Privileges: None. The adversary does not need any authentication or prior access to the system. The vulnerability can be exploited without any credentials or established sessions, making it accessible to completely unauthenticated adversaries who can reach the target system over the network.

User interaction: None. The vulnerability does not require any action from users of the affected system. The adversary can trigger the vulnerability directly through network communication without requiring users to click links, open files, or perform any other actions that would facilitate the attack.

Microsoft ASP.NET Core

rows.CVE Description:
Summary



CVE-2026-50649 is a Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability affecting Microsoft .NET when specific settings are enabled. The vulnerability allows an unauthorized adversary to execute arbitrary code locally on the affected system. Successful exploitation requires user interaction, such as opening a malicious file or document. The vulnerability impacts systems running vulnerable versions of the .NET framework, primarily affecting workstations and servers where .NET applications are deployed. An adversary who successfully exploits this vulnerability can achieve code execution with the privileges of the user who opened the malicious content, potentially leading to full system compromise.



Exploitability




Exploit status: Unproven

Exploit details: The vulnerability stems from improper handling of untrusted data during deserialization operations in .NET. When a .NET application deserializes data from an untrusted source without proper validation, an adversary can craft malicious serialized objects that, when deserialized, execute arbitrary code. The adversary would need to deliver a specially crafted file or data payload to the target system and convince a user to open or process it through a vulnerable .NET application.



Exploit Requirements




Location: On device. The vulnerability can be exploited with local access to the affected device, requiring the adversary to deliver malicious content that is then processed locally by a vulnerable .NET application.

Summary



CVE-2026-50649 is a Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability affecting Microsoft .NET when specific settings are enabled. The vulnerability allows an unauthorized adversary to execute arbitrary code locally on the affected system. Successful exploitation requires user interaction, such as opening a malicious file or document. The vulnerability impacts systems running vulnerable versions of the .NET framework, primarily affecting workstations and servers where .NET applications are deployed. An adversary who successfully exploits this vulnerability can achieve code execution with the privileges of the user who opened the malicious content, potentially leading to full system compromise.



Exploitability




Exploit status: Unproven

Exploit details: The vulnerability stems from improper handling of untrusted data during deserialization operations in .NET. When a .NET application deserializes data from an untrusted source without proper validation, an adversary can craft malicious serialized objects that, when deserialized, execute arbitrary code. The adversary would need to deliver a specially crafted file or data payload to the target system and convince a user to open or process it through a vulnerable .NET application.



Exploit Requirements




Location: On device. The vulnerability can be exploited with local access to the affected device, requiring the adversary to deliver malicious content that is then processed locally by a vulnerable .NET application.

Privileges: None. The adversary does not need any authentication or prior access to the system. However, the adversary must be able to deliver malicious content to the target system and convince a user to interact with it.

User interaction: Required (open file). The vulnerability requires a user to open or process a malicious file or document through a vulnerable .NET application. The adversary cannot trigger the vulnerability directly without user action to process the crafted serialized data.

Conditions: The affected .NET application must perform deserialization operations on untrusted data sources. The application likely needs to be configured to accept and process serialized objects from external or user-controlled sources for the vulnerability to be exploitable.

Microsoft .NET

Summary



CVE-2026-16417 is an Uninitialized Use vulnerability affecting Google Chrome, a web browser developed by Google. The vulnerability exists in the Skia graphics library component of Chrome versions prior to 150.0.7871.182. An adversary who has already compromised the renderer process can exploit this vulnerability to leak cross-origin data by convincing a user to visit a specially crafted HTML page. This results in unauthorized access to sensitive information from other origins, violating the browserâ€™s same-origin policy. The vulnerability affects systems running Google Chrome, including workstations and other devices where the browser is installed.



Exploitability




Exploit status: Unproven

Exploit reliability: The vulnerability requires high attack complexity according to CVSS metrics, suggesting exploitation may be challenging or require specific timing or conditions to succeed reliably

Exploit details: The vulnerability stems from uninitialized memory use in the Skia graphics library. To exploit this, an adversary must first compromise the Chrome renderer process, which handles web page rendering in an isolated sandbox. Once the renderer is compromised, the adversary can craft a malicious HTML page that triggers the uninitialized memory condition in Skia. When the victim visits this page, the vulnerability allows the adversary to read uninitialized memory contents that may contain cross-origin data from other websites or browser contexts. This bypasses Chromeâ€™s same-origin policy protections, potentially exposing sensitive information such as authentication tokens, personal data, or content from other tabs or websites the user has visited.



Exploit Requirements




Location: Remote. The vulnerability can be exploited remotely by an adversary who can convince a user to visit a malicious website, but only after the adversary has already compromised the Chrome renderer process through other means.

Privileges: Renderer process compromise required. The adversary must first compromise the Chrome renderer process before exploiting this vulnerability. This typically requires exploiting a separate vulnerability to gain initial access to the renderer sandbox, after which this vulnerability can be leveraged to leak cross-origin data.

User interaction: Required (visit website). The victim must visit a crafted HTML page controlled by the adversary. The adversary needs to convince the user to navigate to the malicious page, which could be accomplished through phishing, malicious advertisements, or other social engineering techniques.

Conditions: The adversary must have already compromised the renderer process through exploitation of another vulnerability or attack vector. This makes the vulnerability a secondary exploit that requires a prior successful compromise of Chromeâ€™s renderer sandbox.

This requires user interaction, as the victim must visit a malicious website or open a malicious HTML page. Once the renderer process is compromised, the adversary can deliver a specially crafted HTML page that exploits the inappropriate implementation in the Media component. This crafted page bypasses the same origin policy, which is a critical security mechanism that prevents scripts from one origin from accessing data from another origin. The exploitation allows cross-origin access that should normally be blocked by the browserâ€™s security model.



Exploit Requirements




Location: Remote. The vulnerability can be exploited remotely by an adversary who can reach the target system over the network, without requiring local access to the affected device. However, the adversary must first compromise the Chrome renderer process before exploiting this vulnerability.

This represents a significant prerequisite, as the renderer process operates in a sandboxed environment and requires a separate vulnerability or attack vector to compromise.

User interaction: Required (visit website). The victim must visit a malicious website or open a crafted HTML page for the vulnerability to be triggered. The adversary cannot exploit this vulnerability without some form of user interaction that causes the malicious HTML content to be processed by the compromised renderer.

Conditions: The adversary must have already achieved renderer process compromise through other means before this vulnerability can be exploited to bypass same origin policy.

CVE-2026-17899 is a privilege escalation vulnerability affecting Google Chrome, a web browser developed by Google. The vulnerability stems from insufficient policy enforcement in DevTools and affects versions prior to 151.0.7922.72. An adversary who convinces a user to install a malicious Chrome extension can exploit this vulnerability to perform privilege escalation. The vulnerability requires user interaction, specifically the installation of a crafted malicious extension. Successful exploitation allows an adversary to escalate privileges within the browser context, potentially leading to unauthorized access to sensitive data and system resources. This vulnerability primarily affects workstations and devices running Google Chrome.



Exploitability




Exploit status: Unproven

Exploit details: The vulnerability requires an adversary to create a malicious Chrome extension that exploits insufficient policy enforcement in DevTools. Once a user is convinced to install this crafted extension, the adversary can leverage the weakness to escalate privileges beyond what the extension should normally be granted. The exploitation mechanism involves bypassing security policies that should restrict extension capabilities within the DevTools context.



Exploit Requirements





Location: Remote. The vulnerability can be exploited remotely by an adversary who can convince a user to install a malicious Chrome extension, without requiring direct access to the affected device.




Privileges: None. The adversary does not need any authentication or prior access to the system. However, the adversary must successfully convince the user to install a malicious Chrome extension, which serves as the attack vector for privilege escalation.




User interaction: Required (install extension). The vulnerability requires the user to install a malicious Chrome extension crafted by the adversary. Without this user action of installing the malicious extension, the vulnerability cannot be exploited.




Conditions: The affected user must be running a vulnerable version of Google Chrome (prior to 151.0.7922.72) and must install a malicious Chrome extension created by the adversary.

The vulnerability exists in ANGLE (Almost Native Graphics Layer Engine), a graphics abstraction layer used by Chrome to translate OpenGL ES API calls to platform-specific graphics APIs. When specific settings are enabled, a remote adversary can potentially perform a sandbox escape by convincing a user to visit a specially crafted HTML page. The vulnerability affects Google Chrome versions prior to 151.0.7922.72. Successful exploitation could allow an adversary to escape Chromeâ€™s sandbox security boundary, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on the underlying operating system with the privileges of the browser process. This vulnerability primarily affects workstations and devices running the Chrome web browser.

Exploit status: Unproven

Exploit reliability: No public information is available regarding the consistency or reliability of exploitation attempts for this vulnerability

Exploit details: The vulnerability is a type confusion issue in ANGLE, which handles graphics rendering operations. An adversary would need to craft a malicious HTML page that triggers the type confusion condition in ANGLEâ€™s code. When a user visits this crafted page, the browser may incorrectly handle object types during graphics processing, potentially allowing the adversary to manipulate memory in unexpected ways. This memory corruption could be leveraged to bypass Chromeâ€™s sandbox protections, which normally isolate web content from the underlying operating system. The specific technical details of the type confusion and the exact exploitation steps have not been publicly disclosed.

Location: Remote. The vulnerability can be exploited remotely by an adversary who can convince a user to visit a malicious website or open a crafted HTML page, without requiring direct access to the affected device.

CVE-2026-17791 is a UI Spoofing vulnerability affecting Google Chrome, a web browser developed by Google. The vulnerability exists in the Payments component of Chrome prior to version 151.0.7922.72 and stems from insufficient validation of untrusted input. An adversary who has already compromised the renderer process can exploit this vulnerability to perform UI spoofing through a specially crafted HTML page. Successful exploitation allows the adversary to manipulate the user interface, potentially deceiving users into believing they are interacting with legitimate payment interfaces when they are not. This vulnerability affects systems running Google Chrome on desktop platforms including Windows, macOS, and Linux.



Exploitability




Exploit status: Unproven

Exploit details: The vulnerability requires the adversary to first compromise the Chrome renderer process, which is the sandboxed component responsible for rendering web content. Once the renderer process is compromised, the adversary can leverage insufficient input validation in the Payments component to craft malicious HTML pages that spoof legitimate payment user interfaces. This could allow the adversary to create fake payment prompts or dialogs that appear authentic to users, potentially tricking them into entering sensitive payment information or approving fraudulent transactions.



Exploit Requirements





Location: Remote. The vulnerability can be exploited remotely by an adversary who can deliver a crafted HTML page to the victimâ€™s browser, though the adversary must first compromise the renderer process before exploiting this UI spoofing vulnerability.




Privileges: Renderer process compromise required. The adversary must first compromise the Chrome renderer process before exploiting this vulnerability. This typically requires exploiting a separate vulnerability to gain control of the renderer process, after which the UI spoofing can be performed without additional authentication.




User interaction: Required (visit website). The user must visit a website or open an HTML page controlled by the adversary. After the renderer process has been compromised, the user may need to interact with the spoofed payment interface for the attack to achieve its intended impact.




Conditions: The adversary must have already compromised the Chrome renderer process through other means before this UI spoofing vulnerability can be exploited. The Payments feature in Chrome must be accessible for the spoofing to affect payment-related interfaces.

Once the renderer is compromised, the adversary can craft a malicious HTML page that triggers the race condition in the Downloads functionality. By winning this race, the adversary can escape the Chrome sandbox, breaking out of the security boundary that isolates the browser from the rest of the operating system. This would allow the adversary to execute code with the privileges of the Chrome browser process outside the sandbox restrictions.

User interaction: Required (visit website). The user must visit a malicious website or be directed to a crafted HTML page controlled by the adversary. Once the renderer process is compromised, the adversary can trigger the race condition through the malicious page to attempt sandbox escape.

Conditions: The adversary must successfully compromise the Chrome renderer process prior to exploitation. The adversary must also win the race condition for successful sandbox escape, which may require multiple attempts.

CVE-2026-17828 is a UI Spoofing vulnerability affecting Google Chrome for iOS, a web browser for Apple mobile devices. The vulnerability stems from an inappropriate implementation in Chrome for iOS prior to version 151.0.7922.72. An adversary can exploit this flaw by crafting a malicious HTML page that, when visited by a user, allows the adversary to perform UI spoofing attacks. This could enable the adversary to manipulate the user interface in ways that deceive users, potentially leading to phishing attacks or other social engineering schemes. The vulnerability affects mobile devices running Chrome for iOS and requires user interaction to exploit. While the confidentiality and availability of the system remain unaffected, the integrity impact is high, as adversaries can manipulate what users see in the browser interface.

Exploit status: Unproven

Exploit details: The vulnerability requires an adversary to create a specially crafted HTML page that exploits the inappropriate implementation in Chrome for iOS. When a user visits this malicious page, the adversary can manipulate the browserâ€™s user interface elements to display misleading or false information. The specific technical details of the implementation flaw have not been publicly disclosed, but the attack vector involves serving malicious HTML content that triggers the UI spoofing behavior when rendered by the vulnerable Chrome for iOS browser.

Location: Remote. The vulnerability can be exploited remotely by an adversary who can deliver a crafted HTML page to the target user, typically through the internet without requiring access to the same network as the victim.




Privileges: None. The adversary does not need any authentication or prior access to the system. The vulnerability can be exploited without any credentials or established sessions, making it accessible to completely unauthenticated adversaries who can convince users to visit a malicious webpage.




User interaction: Required (visit website). The vulnerability requires the user to visit a malicious website or open a crafted HTML page in Chrome for iOS. Once installed, the malicious extension can leak cross-origin data, allowing the adversary to access information from other websites that should be protected by the browserâ€™s same-origin policy. This vulnerability affects systems running Google Chrome on desktop platforms including Windows, macOS, and Linux. The impact is limited to information leakage with low confidentiality impact, as the adversary can only read certain cross-origin data rather than execute arbitrary code or gain system-level access.

Exploit status: Unproven

The adversary must then use social engineering techniques to convince the target user to install this malicious extension through methods such as phishing, fake extension listings, or other deceptive practices. Once the malicious extension is installed and the user browses websites, the extension can leverage the vulnerability to bypass same-origin policy restrictions and leak cross-origin data from other websites the user visits. The leaked data could include sensitive information from web applications that should be isolated from the extensionâ€™s context.

Privileges: None. The adversary does not need any authentication or prior access to the system. However, the adversary must successfully convince the user to install a malicious Chrome extension through social engineering or other deceptive means.

User interaction: Required (install extension). The vulnerability requires the user to actively install a malicious Chrome extension created by the adversary. The user must go through the extension installation process, which typically involves visiting the Chrome Web Store or loading an unpacked extension, and granting the necessary permissions for the extension to function.

The vulnerability exists in the ANGLE (Almost Native Graphics Layer Engine) component of Google Chrome prior to version 151.0.7922.72. An adversary who has already compromised the renderer process can exploit this vulnerability to potentially perform a sandbox escape via a crafted HTML page when specific settings are enabled. Successful exploitation could allow the adversary to break out of Chromeâ€™s security sandbox, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on the underlying system with elevated privileges. This vulnerability primarily affects workstations and devices running the Google Chrome browser.



Exploitability




Exploit status: Unproven

Exploit reliability: The vulnerability requires the adversary to have already compromised the renderer process, which adds complexity to exploitation. The sandbox escape is deemed potentially achievable through a crafted HTML page, though the exact reliability of the exploit chain is not specified.

Exploit details: The vulnerability is an integer overflow in the ANGLE component of Chrome. To exploit this, an adversary must first compromise the renderer process, which is Chromeâ€™s sandboxed process responsible for rendering web content. Once the renderer is compromised, the adversary can deliver a specially crafted HTML page that triggers the integer overflow in ANGLE. This overflow can be leveraged to escape Chromeâ€™s sandbox security boundary, potentially allowing the adversary to execute code outside the restricted renderer environment and gain access to the underlying operating system with higher privileges.

Privileges: Some privileges required. The adversary must have already compromised Chromeâ€™s renderer process before exploiting this vulnerability. User interaction: Required (visit website). The user must visit a website or open an HTML page controlled by the adversary. However, this user interaction occurs after the adversary has already compromised the renderer process through other means.

Conditions: The adversary must have already compromised the renderer process before this vulnerability can be exploited for sandbox escape. The affected system must be running a vulnerable version of Google Chrome prior to 151.0.7922.72.

Summary



CVE-2026-17900 is an Information Disclosure vulnerability affecting Google Chrome on Windows, a web browser. The vulnerability stems from an inappropriate implementation in the Enterprise component of Google Chrome prior to version 151.0.7922.72. An adversary can exploit this flaw to leak cross-origin data by convincing a user to interact with a malicious file. Successful exploitation results in the disclosure of limited cross-origin information, potentially exposing sensitive data from other web origins. This vulnerability affects Windows-based workstations and devices running the affected Chrome versions. The Chromium security severity for this issue is rated as Low.



Exploitability




Exploit status: Unproven

Exploit reliability: The vulnerability is deemed to have limited impact due to its low confidentiality impact rating and requirement for user interaction, which may affect exploitation consistency in real-world scenarios.



Exploit Requirements




Location: Remote. The vulnerability can be exploited remotely by an adversary who can deliver a malicious file to the target user over the network, without requiring local access to the affected device.

Privileges: None. The adversary does not need any authentication or prior access to the system. The vulnerability can be exploited without any credentials or established sessions, making it accessible to completely unauthenticated adversaries who can reach the target user.

User interaction: Required (open file). The vulnerability requires the user to interact with a malicious file provided by the adversary. The adversary must convince the user to open or process the malicious file, which then triggers the cross-origin data leakage.

Conditions: The affected system must be running Google Chrome on Windows with the Enterprise component enabled.



Affected Products




Google Chrome on Windows: < 151.0.7922.72



Mitigations




Review any recommended remediations

Summary



CVE-2026-17659 is a Site Isolation bypass vulnerability affecting Google Chrome, a web browser developed by Google. The vulnerability stems from an inappropriate implementation in the SiteIsolation component in versions prior to 151.0.7922.72. An adversary who has already compromised the renderer process can exploit this vulnerability to bypass site isolation protections through a specially crafted HTML page. Successful exploitation requires user interaction, as the victim must visit a malicious website containing the crafted HTML page. The vulnerability allows an adversary to potentially access limited information across site boundaries that should normally be isolated, affecting workstations and other devices running the vulnerable Chrome browser versions.



Exploitability




Exploit status: Unproven

Exploit reliability: The exploit requires high attack complexity and depends on the adversary having already compromised the renderer process, which may affect consistency of exploitation

Exploit details: The vulnerability requires the adversary to first compromise the Chrome renderer process, then deliver a specially crafted HTML page to the victim. The crafted HTML page exploits weaknesses in the SiteIsolation implementation to bypass security boundaries that normally prevent different sites from accessing each otherâ€™s data within the browser. The specific technical mechanism involves manipulating how Chrome isolates different origins in separate processes, allowing cross-site information leakage when the renderer process is already under adversary control.



Exploit Requirements




Location: Remote. The vulnerability can be exploited remotely by an adversary who can reach the target system over the network, without requiring local access to the affected device. However, the adversary must first compromise the Chrome renderer process before exploiting this site isolation bypass.

Privileges: Renderer process compromise required. The adversary must have already compromised the Chrome renderer process before exploiting this vulnerability. This represents a significant prerequisite, as the adversary needs existing code execution within the renderer sandbox before the site isolation bypass can be leveraged.

User interaction: Required (visit website). The victim must visit a malicious website or be directed to a crafted HTML page controlled by the adversary. Without this user action to load the malicious content, the vulnerability cannot be triggered even if the renderer process has been compromised.

Conditions: The adversary must have already achieved code execution within the Chrome renderer process through a separate vulnerability or attack vector. This site isolation bypass serves as a secondary exploitation technique to escalate privileges or access beyond the renderer sandbox.

CVE-2026-17781 is an Information Disclosure vulnerability affecting Google Chrome, a web browser developed by Google. The vulnerability stems from an inappropriate implementation in the Extensions component and affects versions prior to 151.0.7922.72. Successful exploitation requires an adversary to convince a user to install a malicious Chrome extension. Once installed, the malicious extension can leak cross-origin data, allowing the adversary to access information from other websites that should be protected by the browserâ€™s same-origin policy. This vulnerability affects systems running Google Chrome on desktop platforms including Windows, macOS, and Linux. The impact is limited to information leakage with low confidentiality impact, as the adversary can only read certain cross-origin data rather than execute arbitrary code or gain system-level access.



Exploitability




Exploit status: Unproven

Exploit details: The vulnerability requires the adversary to create a malicious Chrome extension that exploits the inappropriate implementation in the Extensions API. The adversary must then use social engineering techniques to convince the target user to install this malicious extension through methods such as phishing, fake extension listings, or other deceptive practices. Once the malicious extension is installed and the user browses websites, the extension can leverage the vulnerability to bypass same-origin policy restrictions and leak cross-origin data from other websites the user visits. The leaked data could include sensitive information from web applications that should be isolated from the extensionâ€™s context.



Exploit Requirements




Location: Remote. The vulnerability can be exploited remotely by an adversary who can convince a user to install a malicious Chrome extension, without requiring direct network access to the affected device or local access to the system.

Privileges: None. The adversary does not need any authentication or prior access to the system. However, the adversary must successfully convince the user to install a malicious Chrome extension through social engineering or other deceptive means.

User interaction: Required (install extension). The vulnerability requires the user to actively install a malicious Chrome extension created by the adversary. The user must go through the extension installation process, which typically involves visiting the Chrome Web Store or loading an unpacked extension, and granting the necessary permissions for the extension to function.

Conditions: The affected user must be running a vulnerable version of Google Chrome (prior to 151.0.7922.72) and must install and enable the malicious extension for the vulnerability to be exploitable.

CVE-2026-66315 is a Use After Free vulnerability affecting Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based), a web browser developed by Microsoft. This vulnerability allows an unauthorized adversary to execute arbitrary code on affected systems over a network when specific settings are enabled. The vulnerability requires user interaction to be successfully exploited, as the adversary must convince a user to visit a malicious website or open a specially crafted web page. Successful exploitation could result in remote code execution with the privileges of the logged-in user, potentially compromising workstations and other systems running the vulnerable browser. The vulnerability affects systems where Microsoft Edge is installed and users can be socially engineered to interact with malicious content.



Exploitability




Exploit status: Unproven

Exploit reliability: No public information is available regarding the consistency or reliability of exploits for this vulnerability

Exploit details: The use after free vulnerability occurs when Microsoft Edge improperly handles objects in memory. An adversary could exploit this by hosting a malicious website containing specially crafted content that triggers the use after free condition. When a user visits the malicious site, the browser attempts to access memory that has already been freed, allowing the adversary to execute arbitrary code in the context of the current user. The specific vulnerable code paths and triggering conditions have not been publicly disclosed.



Exploit Requirements




Location: Remote. The vulnerability can be exploited remotely by an adversary who can convince a user to visit a malicious website or open a specially crafted web page, without requiring local access to the affected device.

Privileges: None. The adversary does not need any authentication or prior access to the system. The vulnerability can be exploited without any credentials or established sessions, though the adversary must successfully deliver malicious content to the target user.

User interaction: Required (visit website). The vulnerability requires the user to visit a malicious website or open a specially crafted web page. The adversary must use social engineering techniques such as phishing emails, malicious advertisements, or compromised legitimate websites to convince the user to interact with the malicious content.

Conditions: The affected system must be running a vulnerable version of Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based). The CVSS attack complexity is rated as High, suggesting that successful exploitation may require specific timing conditions or race conditions to be met for the use after free vulnerability to be reliably triggered.

Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based)
